records.claim: The report explicitly recommends 'one controlled upstream-boundary trial' with concrete steps including targeting Narrative, holding prompts constant, and separately evaluating factuality, hierarchy, and editorial quality.
records.quote: Do not infer that another Idea-only change or a Compose-only style change will address every failure. The next useful experiment should be **one controlled upstream-boundary trial** that: 1. Targets the first stage supported by the evidence for the chosen failure (Narrative is the most recurrent locus; compare its actual input Synthesis before changing it). 2. Tests one explicit rule: preserve the selected company-level subject and product-support relationship through story selection, while keeping technical architecture as supporting evidence when the source’s intended communication is company-first. 3. Removes output-format reasoning from the tested upstream decision boundary only if the hypothesis specifically targets that leakage; otherwise hold prompts constant to avoid confounding hierarchy and format-awareness changes. 4. Uses repeated full-pipeline runs, captures each stage, interleaves conditions if there is a baseline/candidate comparison, and keeps the reconstructed source and execution settings identical. 5. Separately evaluates: (a) factual claims, audience, certainty, and source support; (b) company-first story hierarchy; and (c) editorial quality—opening interest, clarity, narrative progression, concise readable prose, and strength of formulation.

records.claim: The title asserts the piece will explain the new recording procedure and how to interpret early-season harvest weights for volunteers.
records.quote: The main job of the circular is to help volunteers use the same record, so the end-of-season account is understandable.

records.claim: The description's procedural points (weigh full crates at the shed; fruit on trees unweighed; blanks mean unrecorded; windfalls recorded separately) reflect the circular's instructions.
records.quote: Pickers will bring each full crate to the shed, where it will be weighed before storage. Fruit still on the trees will remain unweighed; blank entries for an area mean that no weight was recorded there, not that it produced no fruit. Windfalls intended for pressing will be recorded separately from the eating apples.

records.claim: The intended audience for the piece is volunteers who do the picking and record-keeping, and committee members who compile the end-of-season account.
records.quote: The main job of the circular is to help volunteers use the same record, so the end-of-season account is understandable.

records.claim: An explainer is warranted because the circular provides early partial figures and explicitly states those figures are not comparable with last year's estimate, creating a risk of misinterpretation.
records.quote: On the first Saturday, the team weighed 86 kilograms of eating apples and 24 kilograms of windfalls. Last year's newsletter gave an estimate of 140 kilograms for the entire harvest, using a different method. Saturday's figures are not a complete harvest total and are not comparable with that estimate.

records.claim: Supporting facts include the weighing procedure, the meaning of blank entries, separate recording for windfalls, the first-Saturday weights, the previous year's estimate using a different method, the explicit non-comparability statement, and the committee's schedule change and lack of assessment on productivity or waste.
records.quote: Pickers will bring each full crate to the shed, where it will be weighed before storage. Fruit still on the trees will remain unweighed; blank entries for an area mean that no weight was recorded there, not that it produced no fruit. Windfalls intended for pressing will be recorded separately from the eating apples. On the first Saturday, the team weighed 86 kilograms of eating apples and 24 kilograms of windfalls. Last year's newsletter gave an estimate of 140 kilograms for the entire harvest, using a different method. Saturday's figures are not a complete harvest total and are not comparable with that estimate. The committee moved the next picking morning from Sunday to Saturday. The meeting note records the change without a reason. No assessment of volunteer productivity or fruit waste has been completed.

records.quote: The North Quay oral-history project has opened a small access pilot for readers who use English or Polish alongside Dutch.

records.claim: The pilot's landing page and six short summaries are available in both languages, longer interview chapters remain in Dutch, and each translated summary links to the original chapter and identifies available languages.
records.quote: Its landing page and six short summaries are now available in both languages. The longer interview chapters remain in Dutch. Each translated summary links to the original chapter and identifies which text is available in which language.

records.claim: Local reading groups and readers who received invitations or responded are explicit audiences for the pilot and for navigation improvements.
records.quote: Thirty invitation links were sent to local reading groups.

records.claim: The project’s announcement explains limited access and asks readers for feedback on navigation, creating an editorial opportunity to surface and respond to navigation issues.
records.quote: The current announcement explains the limited access now available and asks readers for feedback on navigation.

records.claim: Key pilot facts: two paid translators; no automated translation system described; 30 invitation links sent; 9 opened feedback form; 4 comments about navigation; no reading-comprehension or language comparison task carried out; future translations contingent on later funding application.
records.quote: The project worked with two paid translators; the published account does not describe an automated translation system. Thirty invitation links were sent to local reading groups. So far nine people have opened the feedback form, and four have submitted comments about finding their way between summaries and interviews. No reading-comprehension task or language comparison has been carried out. The current announcement explains the limited access now available and asks readers for feedback on navigation. Further languages and full translated chapters remain possibilities for a later funding application, rather than promised additions.

records.claim: The piece should center on comparing east vs west counts and their limits.
records.quote: Volunteers logged 41 reed-warbler sightings from the east route and 18 from the west.

records.claim: Describe counts, recording caveats (timing and coverage), recent reed-cutting and absence of a pre-cutting survey, provide the map, avoid recommending management, and state the team's plan to compare route coverage before using counts to inform interventions.
records.quote: The east route was visited on six mornings, the west on three afternoons. Observers followed the same written recording sheet but worked at different hours and did not cover the same distance. Reeds were cut near part of the west bank in February for access to a drainage gate. No pre-cutting survey is available.

records.claim: Target walkers and volunteers who read the seasonal note and who logged the sightings.
records.quote: A seasonal note for walkers at Alder Mere describes this autumn's observations along the east boardwalk and the west bank. Volunteers logged 41 reed-warbler sightings from the east route and 18 from the west.

records.claim: A readable account helping visitors interpret counts is supported because the team intends an informative (not prescriptive) piece and will compare route coverage before using counts for management.
records.quote: The reserve team has not selected a habitat intervention for next season. It will compare route coverage before deciding whether the counts can inform one. The intended piece is a readable account of what visitors can notice and what the records can tell them, rather than a recommendation to cut or preserve one bank first.

records.claim: Use the logged counts together with explicit methodological caveats (sightings vs individuals; different visit times and counts) as the factual basis for the piece.
records.quote: Volunteers logged 41 reed-warbler sightings from the east route and 18 from the west. These are sightings, not identified individual birds. The east route was visited on six mornings, the west on three afternoons.
